column7: Redacts header values of a prepared credential; a mistake would silently leak the live token into logs.
Records the declared descriptor mode that later resolution consults; a mistake would silently misclassify an account and bypass the personal/external minting checks.
Wires the transparency logger the mint and refuse paths audit (and fail closed) through; a mistake would silently disable that audit.
Builds the "oauth:{provider}" auth key that the credential check compares against; a mistake would silently accept or reject the wrong account binding.

Decides which callers carry a verified identity: it returns the identity only for a verified proof and None for Operator or Anonymous, so external descriptors and per-user keys are minted only for a caller that proved who it is (siblings classify, new and establishes_the_operator are critical a).
Redacts header values of the propagated credential; a mistake would silently leak the live token into logs.
Redacts the exchanged downstream access_token; a mistake would silently leak the bearer into logs.
Wires the signing key, the assertion strategy and the HTTP client the token exchange authenticates through; a mistake would silently swap the credential or client used.
Refuses a config whose account references do not resolve or whose managed consumers carry a non-account credential, by delegating to compile.
Refuses a managed descriptor lacking the resource/issuer its account key is built from and an external one with no strategy, and builds the compiled identity bindings.
Supplies the method string from_method matches against, so a wrong string silently changes the closed relayed-request set.
Decides whether a JSON-RPC method is in the closed relayed set; None makes the plan refuse UnrecognisedMethod.
Supplies the pending-id prefix that is_bridge_reply_id admits on ingress, so a wrong prefix silently opens or closes the reply gate.
Unconditionally admits every challenge batch, the allow decision when no policy gate is configured.
Mints the unguessable per-prompt wire id and enforces the per-prompt and aggregate wait bounds, ending the call when a peer stalls or answers unusably.
Builds the exact client-visible batch the policy gate inspects, omitting requestState and keys, so a mistake leaves content unscanned.
Builds the final-round result the gate inspects, stripping only requestState, so a mistake leaves content unscanned or scans sealed state.
Refuses a client reply that is an error, lacks a result, or has a missing, declined, unknown or malformed elicitation action instead of filing it for the backend.
Produces the single uniform refusal for every unusable destructive-call confirmation grant, denying the call.
Records the outcome and returns the JSON-RPC error answer that denies the unconfirmed destructive call.
Debug impl redacts hmac_secret_ref; a mistake would silently leak the signing-secret reference into logs.
Builds the ReferenceKey the adapter-vs-gateway alias check compares; returning None wrongly would silently exempt a credential from that check.
Selects which credential is excluded from the alias check; a mistake would silently skip the separation check for a real credential.
Debug impl redacts client_secret_ref; a mistake would silently leak the secret reference.
Per-byte predicate used by validate_session to refuse a session.cookie_name that is not an RFC 6265 token.
Refuses a descriptor carrying authorize_extra outside personal_managed mode rather than silently carrying an inert parameter.
Supplies the default per-principal and gateway-wide journey and store bounds; a wrong value would silently loosen what one principal can consume.
Refuses zero or overflowing store, authority-byte, journey and rate limits at config load so no bound is silently disabled.
Helper that refuses a zero limit value with AccountsConfigError::Limit, called by validate.
Builds the canonicalised env/file identity compared by the structural alias check; a mistake would silently let an adapter alias a gateway credential.
Refuses an absent or empty client_id, redirect_uri or resource value with Unavailable before any request is built.
Allow-lists RFC 6749/7009 error codes so request material or free-text descriptions are never echoed to the operator log; a mistake silently leaks them.
Derives the S256 PKCE challenge from the sealed verifier so the verifier never leaves custody; a mistake silently breaks the PKCE binding.
Refuses a descriptor that leaves send_resource_parameter or resource undeclared instead of defaulting the audience resource.
Builds the one strict client (https-only, no redirects, no proxy, pinning resolver); a mistake silently disables the SSRF and TLS enforcers.
Constructs the reqwest client from the strict builder policy that every outbound call relies on; a mistake would silently drop that policy.
Calls guard (userinfo and SSRF refusal) before any GET is sent, gating the outbound backend call.
Calls guard (userinfo and SSRF refusal) before the token POST is sent, gating the outbound backend call.
The only writer of the transparency-log record for a mint or validation refusal (the decision is mint or validate_and_audit_mint); a mistake silently drops the refusal from the audit trail.
Supplies the default upper bound on an adapter assertion's lifetime that the verifier enforces; a wrong constant silently loosens that bound.
Supplies the default clock skew the assertion verifier tolerates; a wrong constant silently widens the acceptance window.
